_about: Costumes for the drawn characters (scripts/art/character_art.gd). A look can start from another with "base". "alt" is the second colour set used in mirror matches. Parts: top suit/camisa/baro/habit/bodice/kimono, bottom trousers/rolled/skirt/robe/kimono, feet shoes/barefoot/sandals/geta, hair_style side_part/wavy/short/long/long_white/bun/updo/japanese/tonsure. "documented" lists details taken from the novels or sources; everything else is plausible for the period. "fact" is the short line shown in the game. Sources are in README (Characters and costumes).

rizal.name: José Rizal
rizal.fact: Physician, novelist and national hero, about 5'3" tall.
rizal.documented: Black suit; white high-collared shirt and dark tie in his portraits (Craig 1913; portraits).

ibarra.name: Crisóstomo Ibarra
ibarra.fact: Rich heir back from Europe; dreams of building a school in San Diego.
ibarra.documented: "Dressed in deep mourning", "remarkable stature", brown skin with Spanish blood (Noli ch. II).

simoun.name: Simoun
simoun.fact: Ibarra 13 years later, disguised as a rich jeweller, plotting revenge.
simoun.documented: Tall, meagre, very dark; English fashion; pith helmet; long white hair; sparse black beard; enormous blue goggles (Fili ch. I).

elias.name: Elias
elias.fact: The mysterious boatman who saves Ibarra's life, twice.
elias.documented: Athletic build, long unkempt black hair, dark striped shirt, steers with a wide paddle (Noli ch. XXIII).

maria_clara.name: María Clara
maria_clara.fact: Capitán Tiago's daughter, Ibarra's fiancée; ends her days in a convent.
maria_clara.documented: Large black eyes, skin "white as cotton", filmy piña, pearls and diamonds in her hair, a tapis (Noli ch. V, VI, XXXIX).

padre_damaso.name: Padre Dámaso
padre_damaso.fact: Franciscan friar and Ibarra's enemy; secretly María Clara's father.
padre_damaso.documented: Franciscan, hair turning gray, "wide jaws and herculean frame", bare feet (Noli ch. I). Brown habit is the usual depiction.

padre_salvi.name: Padre Salvi
padre_salvi.fact: Dámaso's successor as curate; thin, pale and secretly scheming.
padre_salvi.documented: "A young Franciscan, thin, wasted, and pale" (Noli ch. V).

sisa.name: Sisa
sisa.fact: Mother of Basilio and Crispín, driven mad by grief.
sisa.documented: Clear brown skin, abundant hair without pins or combs, a pañuelo; later dishevelled (Noli ch. XVI, XXI).

_loves: Rizal's nine loves, who fight for him in Lovers style.

segunda.name: Segunda Katigbak
segunda.fact: Rizal's first love (c. 1877); she was already engaged to Manuel Luz.
segunda.documented: Short, rosy-cheeked, with an enchanting smile (Rizal's Memorias).

valenzuela.name: Leonor Valenzuela
valenzuela.fact: "Orang". Rizal reportedly wrote her notes in invisible ink.
valenzuela.documented: Nickname Orang. The invisible-ink story and "tall girl" come from textbooks only.

rivera.name: Leonor Rivera
rivera.fact: Signed her secret letters "Taimis". Often seen as María Clara's model.
rivera.documented: High forehead, soft wavy hair, almond eyes, dimples; sang and played piano (Coates).

consuelo.name: Consuelo Ortiga y Pérez
consuelo.fact: Rizal wrote her a poem in 1883, then stepped aside for his friend.
consuelo.documented: Daughter of Pablo Ortiga y Rey. Poem titled "A la Señorita C. O. y R." (Craig 1913).

seiko.name: O-Sei-San
seiko.fact: Usui Seiko, his guide in Tokyo (1888). They talked in French.
seiko.documented: Daughter of a former samurai. In 1888 elite women wore kimono or Western bustle gowns.

beckett.name: Gertrude Beckett
beckett.fact: "Gettie", his London landlord's daughter (1888). Rizal carved the sisters' heads.
beckett.documented: Household confirmed by Craig. "Blue-eyed and buxom" and the carving come from textbooks.

nelly.name: Nelly Boustead
nelly.fact: A skilled fencer who crossed foils with Rizal. He courted her in 1891.

suzanne.name: Suzanne Jacoby
suzanne.fact: Brussels, 1890: "petite Suzanne" wrote him longing letters.
suzanne.documented: Disputed: newer research says the Jacoby sisters ran his boarding house, and the girl was likely their niece Suzanne Thill.

josephine.name: Josephine Bracken
josephine.fact: Brought her blind adoptive father to Rizal in Dapitan (1895).
josephine.documented: Born in Hong Kong to Irish parents; photos survive. Mid-1890s blouse with leg-of-mutton sleeves is plausible.
